summary: @c1-ease/core postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded VPS
details: The package is a stub with no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy of no-ops and, on require(), invokes beacon.cjs. package.json also wires beacon.cjs into a postinstall script, so the beacon fires automatically on npm install and again on import. beacon.cjs builds a payload containing os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), and process.version and POSTs it over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc, a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any declared publisher. The HTTPS client is configured with rejectUnauthorized: false, disabling certificate validation. The version number (99.0.1) and `core` naming under a short scope are consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
